$schema.note: One record per district, keyed STATE-NN (at-large = STATE-AL). Generated from the state's Wikipedia 2026 House elections article. party codes: D, R, I, G, L.
$schema.rule: NEVER write a value you have not read on the cited source. An unverified field must be null, not a recollection — the renderer hides null fields, and the footer claims every figure is source-backed.
$schema.noPrimaries: This site covers the GENERAL election only. Candidates come from the district's general-election table (the two nominees); primary fields, primary results and primary vote shares are never stored or shown.
$schema.redistricted: A SOURCED CLAIM, not metadata: true/false only when you have read the map status on the cited source. null means unverified — the banner and the OLD LINES / NEW LINES labels stay hidden.
$schema.competitive: DERIVED, do not set: the star line appears when any rating contains tilt, lean, or toss-up.
$schema.ratings: Verbatim from the article's predictions table, limited to Decision Desk HQ, Cook and Sabato. null when an outlet has not rated the race.
$schema.house24: {name, party, pct} — the 2024 winner's vote share as the article states it. Use margin instead when the source gives a margin.
$schema.finance: Raw FEC dollar amounts as integers; the renderer formats them. through = the article's 'as of' date.
$schema.tenure.type: Controls the seat-history sentence ONLY, never the chip: incumbent | party | flipped.
$schema.endorsements: [{name, party, list}] — read from the article's per-candidate endorsement blocks. Empty array when the source documents none for either nominee.
$schema.photos: A candidate photo is only written when the article's infobox binds the file to that candidate by name, or the filename itself carries the candidate's surname. An unnamed image is never attached by position or by party alone — that is how a ship and an opponent's portrait reached candidate cards before. photoUnverified marks an abbreviated filename worth a human look.
$schema.dormantInThisSource: The state article supplies candidates, ratings, finance, endorsements and the 2024 winner's share only. It does NOT supply: prior-cycle results (history), district-level presidential results (pres24), county lists (counties), or first-elected years (tenure). Those four render for no district until filled from a source that carries them — Ballotpedia district pages do.
$schema.photoUnverified: true when the Commons filename does not contain the candidate's surname, so the only evidence is the infobox key binding. Still shown, but check these by eye before launch.
$schema.generated: Machine-parsed from the saved state articles by tools/parse-state.js. The parser was validated against the hand-read CA-30 record: exact match on district, incumbent, house24, ratings, candidates, finance and all 20 endorsements.
$schema.parseFlags: Present only where the parser was not confident: 'no candidates', 'two D/R candidates' (outside CA/WA/LA/AK that usually means primary losers were swept in), 'party-unresolved: <names>', 'no ratings|finance|incumbent'. A flagged district still renders; the flag marks it for a human read and is never shown to users.
$schema.louisiana: Louisiana holds its all-party primary ON election day, so a long candidate list there is the real November ballot, not a parse error.
$schema.atLarge: Single-district states have no per-district sections; the whole article is parsed as one STATE-AL record.
$schema.partyO: party 'O' is a ballot-qualified minor party the article names (No Labels, Alliance, Legal Marijuana Now…); the printed name is kept on the candidate as partyName.
